A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the performance of the rectangular subimage method on a MIMD machine is comparable to the performance of the stripe subimage method on an SIMD machine, but the rectangular method is much more efficient than the stripe method on a mixed-mode parallel machine.

a parallel implementation on a distributed memory SIMD machine can be more effective than a parallel implementation on an MIMD machine for a class of applications, such as the block-based motion vector estimation problem.
, for this application task and for the range of problem sizes considered, a mixed mode of execution (SIMD and SPMD) is more effective than either SIMD or SPMD execution alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of a parallel algorithm can vary dramatically depending on the parallel processing system used.

, while the performance of a parallel algorithm on a single parallel machine may be good, the performance of a heterogeneous suite of machines can be significantly worse, and that the choice of a particular parallel machine or a suite of machines for a specific application can be very important.
the choice of the best mapping strategy is highly dependent on the characteristics of the target machine.
